fueleu: FuelEU Maritime (Regulation (EU) 2023/1805) has applied since 1 January 2025. It sets a limit on the greenhouse gas intensity of the energy a ship uses over a year, 89.34 grams of CO2 equivalent per megajoule from 2025 (2 percent under the 91.16 reference), and a penalty of EUR 2,400 per tonne of VLSFO equivalent energy in deficit. It is settled per ship and year, with banking, borrowing and pooling, so a single voyage has no penalty of its own: the figures below are the penalty the voyage's energy would carry if the ship burnt the same fuel all year, shown beside the TCE and kept out of it.
method: Emissions are the fuel burnt by grade times the factors of the MRV Regulation (EU) 2015/757 as amended: 3.114 t of CO2 per t of HFO, 3.151 for LFO and 3.206 for MGO, with VLSFO an ISO 8217 residual grade (HFO). From 2026 methane and nitrous oxide count, at 0.00005 and 0.00018 g per g of fuel times warming potentials of 28 and 265.

Covered emissions follow Article 3ga of the ETS Directive: 100 percent of a voyage between two EEA ports and of the time at berth in them, 50 percent of a voyage into or out of the EEA. Allowances are surrendered for 40 percent of 2024 emissions, 70 percent of 2025 and 100 percent from 2026 (Article 3gb).
